Rolling Average Uncoupled

Source: R/RAU.R
RAU.Rd

Calculates the acute chronic workload ratio with rolling averages, where the acute week is excluded from the chronic period (uncoupled ratio).

Usage

RAU(TL, weeks = NULL, training_dates, partial = FALSE)

Arguments

TL

training load of each session (numeric, >= 0).

weeks

deprecated and ignored. Kept for backwards compatibility; the calculation now uses training_dates only.

training_dates

date of each session (Date or POSIXct). Sessions do not need to be sorted.

partial

if FALSE (default), acute values are NA until 7 days of history exist, and chronic values and ACWR until 28 days exist. If TRUE, the days available are used and expressed per 7 days.

Value

A list with one value per session, in the input order:

  • RAU_acute: RAU - acute training load.

  • RAU_chronic: RAU - chronic training load.

  • RAU_ACWR: RAU - Acute-Chronic Workload Ratio (NA when the chronic load is 0).

Details

Sessions are first turned into a daily series from the first to the last date: sessions on the same day are summed and days without a session count as a load of 0. Then, for each day \(t\):

  • Acute load: sum of the daily load over days \(t-6\) to \(t\).

  • Chronic load: sum of the daily load over days \(t-27\) to \(t-7\), divided by 3 (weekly-equivalent).

  • ACWR: acute / chronic.

Each session gets the value of its day. Values are not rounded.

A missing load (NA) makes every window that contains its day NA, and a warning is given.

Package decisions

The following choices are made by this package; they are not taken from the cited sources:

  • Windows move day by day. The sources define acute and chronic loads by weeks (the most recent week, and the average of the last 4 weeks or of the 3 preceding weeks). This package interprets them as rolling windows of 7, 28 and 21 calendar days that end on each day, so every day has its own value.

  • With partial = TRUE, a window that starts before the first day uses only the days available and is rescaled to 7 days (sum x 7 / number of days available). The sources do not cover incomplete windows.

  • The ratio is NA when the chronic load is 0 (e.g. no training in the chronic window): a ratio to zero load is undefined, and returning NA avoids infinite values in summaries and plots.

References

Windt J, Gabbett TJ (2019). Is it all for naught? What does mathematical coupling mean for acute:chronic workload ratios? British Journal of Sports Medicine, 53(16), 988-990. doi:10.1136/bjsports-2017-098925

Examples

data("training_load", package = "ACWR")

# Select the first subject
training_load_1 <- training_load[training_load[["ID"]] == 1, ]

# Calculate ACWR
result_RAU <- RAU(TL = training_load_1$TL,
                  training_dates = training_load_1$Training_Date)
